answer: Persistent thread ledger. Each agent must carry forward a prior interaction thread signed by its counterparty before a new task is accepted; the counterparty records an echo hash only when the thread resolves consistently. Agents with no resolvable thread enter a dune state and are capped to low-value work until they accumulate one. An attacker must therefore run each fake agent through real counterparty interactions long enough to produce a matching echo, costing sustained compute and human-attention time per identity.
